newsitem.title: SWEDEN: S-E-Banken, Nordbanken to merge next week - paper.
newsitem.headline: S-E-Banken, Nordbanken to merge next week - paper.

text.p: A merger between Swedish banks S-E-Banken and state-controlled Nordbanken will soon be ready, and could be announced as early as next week, Swedish daily Dagens Nyheter said on Friday.

Citing sources, the newspaper said signs that a merger is about to happen include reports that investments from both banks have been stopped and top managers from S-E-Banken have been asked to cancel any travel plans.

Contacted by Reuters, neither bank would comment on the report. "According to Dagens Nyheter reports, all investments, even previously decided ones, are stopped in the two banks," Dagens Nyheter said.
"In addition, both have a general freeze on hiring and there are reports that managers within S-E-Banken have been instructed to cancel any travel plans," the newspaper said.
"In addition the instructions from the bank's board are to be prepared for any possible organisational changes in the beginning of the year," it said.
The two banks have held comprehensive discussions, other sources told the newspaper.
"The conclusion of these is that a merger is a good idea," Dagens Nyheter said.

It is rumoured that Nordbanken managing director Hans Dalborg would become managing director of the merged bank while the current managing director of S-E-Banken, Bjorn Svedberg, would become head of the board, the newspaper said.

Rumours of a shake-up in the Swedish banking sector have been circulating for several months, with reports repeatedly naming S-E-Banken and Nordbanken as possible merger partners as well as Foreningsbanken and Swedbank in another merger deal.
Nordbanken is 59 percent owned by the state.
